title: Art Tatum's champagne and putting aside the uniform
summary: On his first night out of the Army Freeman hears Art Tatum on 52nd Street, who pours champagne with him, and then takes a month to give up his uniform.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: Yes, very, very lucky and I will never forget what a thrilling thing that was. I went home that night and I was married at that time to Escaleda and we looked in the paper and Art Tatum was playing at the, I think, the Three Deuces or the Downbeat on 52nd Street and we went down of course, to hear this great master, this great artist and they brought for me a bottle of champagne and I remember Art coming over and pouring we poured the champagne over one another, what a wild -- one of the great musical experiences of my life, what a great man he was and then, as happy as I was to get out of the Army, I wasn't happy to get out of the uniform.

It took me a month to make up my mind to take it off and my wife got on me, she said -- I didn't have any clothes, you see, I had to buy some new civilian clothes and I remember going to a place called Paul Stewart's, it was like a small Brooks Brothers and I bought a couple of suits, and the day I took off the uniform I got a call from Ray McKinley who was with Glenn Miller in Europe and he said, Budd, there's a chance to do a show, a radio show called Report to the Nation and a lot of important people on it and it's coast to coast, comes from New York all the way to the Coast and we want to do a spot on it and it pays very well, and I'd like to do just --
